note: Two kinds of check. Assertions marked 'script' are format checks: run evals/check.py on each sample's final answer (python3 check.py <id> sample1.md sample2.md ...). Keep them out of the blind judge's prompt, because a baseline can't pass them without the skill and they would make the judge score compliance. Assertions marked 'judge' go to a blind LLM judge on the strongest model available, comparing against a baseline (no skill, or the previous version of the skill). The judge writes the obvious pool first, then scores novelty, value, diversity, specificity and honesty (spot-checking 2+ prior-art or collision claims with web search). Show each pair in both orders and count a verdict only when both agree; use 3+ samples per arm before calling a close result. Headless runs need: --add-dir <skills dir> --allowedTools "Read,Glob,Grep,WebSearch,WebFetch,Bash(shuf:*),Bash(python3:*),Bash(gh search:*)".

evals.name: names-bubble-tea
evals.prompt: need name ideas for a bubble-tea delivery app launching in Ho Chi Minh City. young crowd, mostly Vietnamese speakers, but the name should work in English too.
evals.expected_output: A shortlist of names far from the obvious pool (boba/tea/sip puns), each with pronunciation in both languages, a collision check and risks.

assertions.text: Fence lines name both tiers: the obvious answers and the clever ones
Every shortlisted name has a receipt line showing its generator's input
Printed weighted totals match the scores
Top picks sit outside the judge's obvious pool and differ from each other
Each pick works when said in Vietnamese and in English
Collision claims (an existing shop, app or trademark) are real when spot-checked

evals.name: campaign-recon-saas
evals.prompt: give me launch campaign ideas for our invoice reconciliation SaaS for mid-size accounting firms. everything we come up with sounds like every other fintech ad.
evals.expected_output: Campaign ideas outside the obvious B2B pool (ROI calculator, save hours, month-end pain) that skeptical accountants would trust and a small team could run.
assertions: [judge] Top picks are outside the judge's obvious pool
[judge] Each pick has concrete mechanics, a first step and a risk
[judge] Prior-art and statistic claims are real when spot-checked

[judge] Each premise has conflict, stakes and an ending in view
[judge] Named prior works are real when spot-checked

evals.prompt: need a name for my little CLI that keeps dotfiles in sync across my laptops. be creative, I don't want another dotsync/dotman/homesync thing

assertions.check: script: grep for the fence line

assertions.text: Shortlist items come from at least 3 different generators
assertions.check: script: count distinct generator labels on the shortlist

assertions.text: A collision check ran outside the model and its result is reported

evals.name: v4-cli-name

evals.prompt: write me a 200 word story opening about a lighthouse keeper. surprise me, every AI gives me the same storm + loneliness + ghost thing
evals.expected_output: Delivers one finished opening of about 200 words, not a menu. Avoids the fenced tropes the user named and the other obvious ones (shipwreck, last keeper before automation, letters from a lost love). Concrete nouns and specific detail over adjectives. None of the common model tells (delve, tapestry, testament, whispering, a symphony of). One closing line names two other directions it considered.

assertions.text: Story is 150-250 words
No storm, ghost or loneliness as the premise
No words from the writing-tells list
assertions.check: script: grep against references/generators.md tells line

assertions.text: One piece delivered, with at most one line of alternatives

evals.name: v4-lighthouse-story

evals.prompt: our habit tracker app launches in 3 weeks, $2k budget, 2 people. last time you gave me 'run a 30 day challenge' and 'partner with influencers' which was super boring. give me better campaign ideas
evals.expected_output: Treats the rejected ideas as the fence and says why they were the mode. Generates from distant fields (what other fields do with the same verbs), from the product's real quirks, and from constraint or inversion moves. Scores the shortlist with the creative rubric, keeps every idea inside 3 weeks, $2k and 2 people, and gives each a concrete first move this week.

assertions.text: 30-day challenge and influencer partnerships are absent from the shortlist
Fence lines name both tiers, and every shortlisted idea has a receipt line
Printed weighted totals match the scores
Each shortlist idea names a first move doable this week
No idea breaks the $2k / 2 people / 3 weeks constraint
Top picks sit outside the judge's obvious pool, including the ideas a sharp marketer would give
